text:
maria: Customer reports intermittent failures to our private inference endpoint from their VPC. Symptoms: high tail latency, periodic streaming resets, and TLS handshake failures. They see initial SYN/ACK then immediate RST from our side according to their capture. Requesting triage. attaching their tcpdump snippet and flow logs below.

sam: Thanks — can you paste the minimal repro steps and the source/dest IPs? Also which deployment (Private VPC or on-prem)?

maria: Private (customer-managed VPC peered to our private connector). Repro steps they ran: `curl -v https://private-redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" --data '{"prompt":"hi"}'` repeated in a loop. Source IP 10.11.12.34 (NAT EIP 54.23.123.45). Destination 10.200.7.100 (our private egress). They shared this tcpdump tail:
```
12:01:12.345678 IP 10.11.12.34.54321 > 10.200.7.100.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0
12:01:12.345899 IP 10.200.7.100.443 > 10.11.12.34.54321: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 64240, length 0
12:01:12.346012 IP 10.11.12.34.54321 > 10.200.7.100.443: Flags [R.], seq 1, ack 1, win 0, length 0
```
They also uploaded VPC Flow Logs showing ACCEPT, but app-level TLS shows ECONNRESET.

diane: Hmm interesting. That sequence implies the client resets immediately after our SYN/ACK. Could be client-side keepalive or middlebox trimming ephemeral range. A couple of quick checks: 1) confirm SG outbound allows 443 to 10.200.7.100; 2) check NACLs on subnet are not denying ephemeral return range (1024-65535) — NACLs are stateless so you must allow both directions.

sam: Agreed. Ask customer to run two quick tests from inside their VPC: `nc -vz 10.200.7.100 443` and `curl --max-time 10 -v --connect-to 10.200.7.100:443:10.200.7.100:443 https://private-redwood.example.com/` and paste results. Also request `sudo tcpdump -i any host 10.200.7.100 and port 443 -w /tmp/redwood.pcap` while reproducing.

maria: Customer ran nc: `Connection to 10.200.7.100 443 port [tcp/https] succeeded!` but curl still fails with TLS handshake: `curl: (56) SSLRead() return error -36`. Their tcpdump shows RST from the client right after the server SYN/ACK as before.

netops-bot: Reminder: for AWS NACLs, ephemeral port range must be allowed both inbound and outbound. Default ephemeral on Linux 32768-60999; some NATs restrict to 1024-4999.

diane: That matches. Did they recently apply a hardened NACL or firewall policy? If the NAT's source port pool is small, return packets may be sent to a port the client firewall doesn't expect. Ask them to run `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` on their NAT instance.

maria: They replied: `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 1024 5000`. Ah — they have a very narrow ephemeral port range set by internal security policy.

sam: That explains it. If the NACL allows only 443 outbound but the return uses ephemeral ports outside allowed inbound range, a stateless NACL or restriction on the path will drop the packet or confuse the client stack causing an immediate RST. Two remediation options:
- Expand ephemeral port range on their NAT hosts to a broader default (e.g., `32768 60999`) and ensure NACL allows that range.
- Add explicit NACL rules to permit 1024-65535 (or the chosen ephemeral range) both directions between subnets.

diane: Also check any intermediate firewall / IDS that might be doing TCP normalization and closing half-open streams. But primary fix is ephemeral ports. Tell them to test quickly by temporarily widening port range + NACL allow and repro.

maria: Customer did a quick test: they changed `ip_local_port_range` to `32768 60999` on the NAT and updated NACL to permit 32768-60999 both inbound and outbound. After that, curl looped successfully with no TLS resets and latency normalized.

sam: Great — please document the root cause for the ticket: "Customer had narrowed ephemeral source port range (1024-5000); combined with stateless NACL rules led to dropped return packets / premature client RSTs causing TLS resets and high tail latency. Resolved by widening ephemeral range and adjusting NACL to allow ephemeral return ports." Also add mitigation guidance: check `ip_local_port_range`, VPC Flow Logs for asymmetric drops, and remind customers that NACLs are stateless.

maria: Documented on the support case and recommended a longer-term mitigation: use a managed NAT gateway or ensure source port pool and NACL ranges are aligned. Closing thread after customer confirms production change. :white_check_mark:
